text.en: A young cart driver at the docks loved oranges so much that one day they got him into trouble.

The narrator drove a pony-and-cart for the Swift Delivery Company and often went in and out of the docks. He was not a real thief, but he often picked up fruit that fell from the boats and hid it under a big apron. Clem Jones planned thefts carefully, but the narrator took things only when he found them, until a policeman found seventeen oranges hidden in his pockets.
The story is humorous but it carries a clear moral: even small dishonest acts can have big consequences. It also shows the difference between a careful planner and an opportunist, and how the narrator never ate an orange again after being locked up.
Note the colloquial, first-person style and words like docks, apron, pony-and-cart, theft and planner.
